title: Two very different glowing gas clouds in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: The gas clouds NGC 2014 and NGC 2020, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: Henize 55, Large Magellanic Cloud, NGC 2014, NGC 2020 · constellation Dorado · about 160000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two glowing clouds of gas sit side by side in this sharp view of a region of star birth in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small galaxy orbiting the Milky Way. On the right, NGC 2014 is irregular in shape and red. Its neighbor, NGC 2020, is round and blue.

They look very different, yet both were shaped in the same basic way. Extremely hot newborn stars drive powerful stellar winds that sculpt the surrounding gas. Those same stars also pour radiation into the gas, making it glow brightly.

The caption does not explain why they differ in shape and color, but the pair shows how the same forces can produce very different results. The Very Large Telescope recorded the scene through broad filters and narrow ones for oxygen and hydrogen.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.17 x 7.17 arcminutes) and distance (160000 light years), the frame spans roughly 334 × 334 light-years. Its light set out about 160,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the FORS2 instrument on the Very Large Telescope, using B, V and R filters plus filters for oxygen and hydrogen light. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Long exposures on a large telescope gather much more light than the eye, so these faint clouds look far brighter here than they would by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
